literal: He Bayun; Cai Jun; Han Xian; Wei Zhangming; Wang Huai; Liu Gui; Ren Yanjing; Moduoluo Daiwen; Gao Shigui; Shidi Huiluo; Shidi Sheng; Xue Guyan; Zhang Baoluo; Houmo Chenxiang
idiomatic: He Bayun; Cai Jun; Han Xian; Wei Zhangming; Wang Huai; Liu Gui; Ren Yanjing; Moduoluo Daiwen; Gao Shigui; Shidi Huiluo; Shidi Sheng; Xue Guyan; Zhang Baoluo; Houmo Chenxiang

literal: He Bayun, styled Kenui, was a native of Jianshan in Shenwu.
idiomatic: He Bayun, styled Kenui, was a native of Jianshan in Shenwu.

literal: His grandfather Ertou and his father Dubá are both recorded in the Wei History.
idiomatic: His grandfather Ertou and his father Dubá are both recorded in the Wei History.

literal: Bayun was skilled with bow and horse and possessed considerable daring and resource; with his younger brother Yue he killed the bandit chief Wei Kehong, then fled to Wei.
idiomatic: He Bayun excelled with bow and horse and possessed considerable daring; with his younger brother Yue he killed the bandit chief Wei Kehong, then fled to Wei.

literal: Prince Yuanshen of Guangyang recommended Bayun as General of Accumulated Archers, with staff of authority defending Fukou.
idiomatic: Prince Yuanshen of Guangyang recommended He Bayun as general of accumulated archers, bearer of the staff of authority defending Fukou.

literal: When Yuanshen was defeated, he returned to Erzhu Rong.
idiomatic: When Yuanshen was defeated, he returned to Erzhu Rong.

literal: Bayun, his father, his sons, and his brothers were all known for martial skill; Rong had long heard of them.
idiomatic: He Bayun, his father, his sons, and his brothers were all known for martial skill; Erzhu Rong had long heard of them.

literal: When he met Bayun, he treated him with great generosity.
idiomatic: When he met He Bayun, he treated him with great generosity.

literal: At the beginning of Jianyi, Bayun was appointed General Who Subdues the East and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, enfeoffed Marquis of Shouyang County with a fief of seven hundred households.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianyi, He Bayun was appointed general who subdues the east and grand master of splendid happiness, enfeoffed marquis of Shouyang County with a fief of seven hundred households.

literal: During Yongan, he was appointed General Who Subdues the North and Governor of Weizhou, and his rank was advanced to Duke.
idiomatic: During Yongan, he was appointed general who subdues the north and governor of Weizhou, and his rank was advanced to duke.

literal: When the Prince of Changguang of Wei was enthroned, Bayun's title was changed to Duke of Yan Commandery, and he was made concurrent Palace Attendant.
idiomatic: When the Prince of Changguang of Wei was enthroned, He Bayun's title was changed to duke of Yan Commandery, and he was made concurrent palace attendant.

literal: Sent on mission to the Rouran, on his return he reached Jinyang just as the Grand Ancestor was about to march east out of Shandong; Bayun had long known the Grand Ancestor was no ordinary man and had early pledged himself to him.
idiomatic: Sent on mission to the Rouran, on his return he reached Jinyang just as Gao Huan was about to march east out of Shandong; He Bayun had long known Gao Huan was no ordinary man and had early pledged himself to him.

literal: The Grand Ancestor, because Bayun was a man of standing among the northern gentry, treated him with especial affection and honor.
idiomatic: Because He Bayun was a man of standing among the northern gentry, Gao Huan treated him with especial affection and honor.

literal: He then went out from Xindu with Bayun to settle the great plan.
idiomatic: He then went out from Xindu with He Bayun to settle the great plan.

literal: At the beginning of Wei Zhongxing, Bayun was transferred to Minister over the Masses and held concurrently the office of Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Wei Zhongxing, He Bayun was transferred to minister over the masses and held concurrently the office of director of the masters of writing.

literal: When the Grand Ancestor entered Luoyang, Bayun's rank was advanced to Prince, he was transferred to Grand Commandant, and made additionally Palace Attendant.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan entered Luoyang, He Bayun's rank was advanced to prince, he was transferred to grand commandant, and made additionally palace attendant.

literal: When Emperor Wu of Wei was suspicious of the Grand Ancestor, because Bayun's younger brother Yue was deeply entrusted to him, they secretly sent messengers back and forth.
idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Wei was suspicious of Gao Huan, because He Bayun's younger brother Yue was deeply entrusted to him, they secretly sent messengers back and forth.

literal: At the time all feared Bayun would turn traitor.
idiomatic: At the time all feared He Bayun would turn traitor.

literal: When Yue died, Emperor Wu again entrusted Yue's younger brother Sheng with the most intimate confidence.
idiomatic: When Yue died, Emperor Wu again entrusted Yue's younger brother Sheng with the most intimate confidence.

literal: The Grand Ancestor, valuing their old ties, long protected him intact.
idiomatic: Gao Huan, valuing their old ties, long protected him intact.

literal: Only in the first year of Tianping was Bayun granted death by imperial decree; he was forty-eight, and the Grand Ancestor came in person to mourn.
idiomatic: Only in the first year of Tianping was He Bayun granted death by imperial decree; he was forty-eight, and Gao Huan came in person to mourn.

literal: Posthumously he was granted Governor of Ding Province and command over military affairs in five provinces.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted governor of Ding Province and command over military affairs in five provinces.

literal: Bayun had three sons: the eldest Shiwen, the second Shile, and the third Nantuo.
idiomatic: He Bayun had three sons: the eldest Shiwen, the second Shile, and the third Nantuo.

literal: At the end of Xinghe, the Grand Ancestor summoned them all to study together with his own sons.
idiomatic: At the end of Xinghe, Gao Huan summoned them all to study together with his own sons.

literal: During Wuding, an edict ordered them to reside in Ding Province and granted them fields and dwellings.
idiomatic: During Wuding, an edict ordered them to reside in Ding Province and granted them fields and dwellings.

literal: Cai Jun, styled Jingyan, was a native of Shimen in Guangning.
idiomatic: Cai Jun, styled Jingyan, was a native of Shimen in Guangning.

literal: His father Pu, when the north was in turmoil, fled to Wuyuan; in garrison and battle he had merit.
idiomatic: His father Pu, when the north was in turmoil, fled to Wuyuan; in garrison and battle he had merit.

literal: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and enfeoffed Baron of Anshang County with a fief of two hundred households.
idiomatic: He was appointed general who pacifies the north and enfeoffed baron of Anshang County with a fief of two hundred households.

literal: Soon after he died and was posthumously granted General Who Assists the State and Governor of Yan Province.
idiomatic: Soon after he died and was posthumously granted general who assists the state and governor of Yan Province.

literal: Jun was bold and generous with courage; when the Grand Ancestor was still obscure, Jun attached himself deeply to him.
idiomatic: Cai Jun was bold and generous with courage; when Gao Huan was still obscure, he attached himself deeply to him.

literal: Together with Duan Chang of Liaoxi and Pang Cangying of Taiyuan, he possessed the discerning eye of one who sees ahead.
idiomatic: Together with Duan Chang of Liaoxi and Pang Cangying of Taiyuan, he possessed the discerning eye of one who sees ahead.

literal: Chang was commandant of Huashuo garrison in Wei; once when he saw the Grand Ancestor he found him very remarkable and said to him: "You have the talent to bring order to the age; in the end you will not come to nothing — please accept my descendants as a trust.
idiomatic: Chang was commandant of Huashuo garrison in Wei; once when he saw Gao Huan he found him very remarkable and said to him: "You have the talent to bring order to the age; in the end you will not come to nothing — please accept my descendants as a trust.

literal: " In Xinghe, the Grand Ancestor memorialized to posthumously grant Chang Duke of Works.
idiomatic: " In Xinghe, Gao Huan memorialized to posthumously grant Chang duke of works.

literal: His son Ning was aide in the chief minister's headquarters; at the beginning of Tianbao he was made concurrently General of the Southern Central Cadres.
idiomatic: His son Ning was aide in the chief minister's headquarters; at the beginning of Tianbao he was made concurrently general of the southern central cadres.

literal: Cangying consorted with bold knights-errant and treated traveling guests generously; he lived in the prefectural city.
idiomatic: Pang Cangying consorted with bold knights-errant and treated traveling guests generously; he lived in the prefectural city.

literal: The Grand Ancestor lodged at his house; at first he dwelt in a snail-shell hut, and Cangying's mother several times saw red vapor on the hut reaching to heaven.
idiomatic: Gao Huan lodged at his house; at first he dwelt in a snail-shell hut, and Cangying's mother several times saw red vapor on the hut reaching to heaven.

literal: Cangying too knew the Grand Ancestor had the measure of a hegemon-king; he always privately showed him extra respect, ceded half his house to serve the Grand Ancestor, and thereby came to receive personal recognition.
idiomatic: Cangying too knew Gao Huan had the measure of a hegemon-king; he always privately showed him extra respect, ceded half his house to serve Gao Huan, and thereby came to receive personal recognition.

literal: When the Grand Ancestor governed Jin Province, he brought Cangying in as concurrent aide-de-camp administrative secretary and charged him with the affairs of Yining Commandery.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan governed Jin Province, he brought Cangying in as concurrent aide-de-camp administrative secretary and charged him with the affairs of Yining Commandery.

literal: When the banner of righteousness was raised, Cangying abandoned his household and traveled secretly by side paths to rejoin the Grand Ancestor; the Grand Ancestor made him concurrent director of the granary section in the mobile office.
idiomatic: When the banner of righteousness was raised, Cangying abandoned his household and traveled secretly by side paths to rejoin Gao Huan; Gao Huan made him concurrent director of the granary section in the mobile office.

literal: He died while serving as Governor of An Province.
idiomatic: He died while serving as governor of An Province.

literal: Jun was at first captured by Du Luozhou; at the time the Grand Ancestor was also in Luozhou's army; the Grand Ancestor plotted to kill Luozhou, and Jun took part in the plan.
idiomatic: Cai Jun was at first captured by Du Luozhou; at the time Gao Huan was also in Luozhou's army; Gao Huan plotted to kill Luozhou, and Cai Jun took part in the plan.

literal: When the affair was exposed, he fled to Ge Rong, then turned against Ge and went over to Erzhu Rong.
idiomatic: When the affair was exposed, he fled to Ge Rong, then turned against Ge and went over to Erzhu Rong.

literal: When Rong entered Luoyang, Jun was made General Who Pacifies the Distance and a separate commander within the headquarters guard.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang, Cai Jun was made general who pacifies the distance and a separate commander within the headquarters guard.

literal: He followed in the defeat of Ge Rong and was appointed Grand Advisor for Remonstrance.
idiomatic: He followed in the defeat of Ge Rong and was appointed grand advisor for remonstrance.

literal: He also followed in the pacification of Yuan Hao and was enfeoffed Baron of Wuluo County.
idiomatic: He also followed in the pacification of Yuan Hao and was enfeoffed baron of Wuluo County.

literal: He followed the Grand Ancestor in raising righteousness and was made Area Commander.
idiomatic: He followed Gao Huan in raising righteousness and was made area commander.

literal: When the Grand Ancestor pacified Ye and when he defeated the Four Huns at Hanling, Jun had military merit in both.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan pacified Ye and when he defeated the Four Huns at Hanling, Cai Jun had military merit in both.

literal: During Taichang he went out as Governor of Ji Province; his governance was harsh and violent and he accepted many bribes, yet he was also clear-minded and had method, and officials and commoners feared and obeyed him.
idiomatic: During Taichang he went out as governor of Ji Province; his governance was harsh and violent and he accepted many bribes, yet he was also clear-minded and had method, and officials and commoners feared and obeyed him.

literal: By nature he loved entertaining guests and was noted for generous giving.
idiomatic: By nature he loved entertaining guests and was noted for generous giving.

literal: Later Hu Qian and others seized Yan Province in rebellion; Jun together with Wei Jing, Governor of Qi Province, suppressed and pacified them.
idiomatic: Later Hu Qian and others seized Yan Province in rebellion; Cai Jun together with Wei Jing, governor of Qi Province, suppressed and pacified them.

literal: Emperor Wu of Wei was disloyal to the Grand Ancestor; because Ji Province was strategically vital, he wished to place a trusted confidant in command there.
idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Wei was disloyal to Gao Huan; because Ji Province was strategically vital, he wished to place a trusted confidant in command there.

literal: He secretly ordered censors to fabricate charges against Jun, intending to replace Jun with the Prince of Ruyang, and for this reason Jun was transferred to administer Yan Province affairs.
idiomatic: He secretly ordered censors to fabricate charges against Cai Jun, intending to replace him with the Prince of Ruyang, and for this reason Cai Jun was transferred to administer Yan Province affairs.

literal: The Grand Ancestor, holding that Jun was not guilty, memorialized to restore him to his post.
idiomatic: Gao Huan, holding that Cai Jun was not guilty, memorialized to restore him to his post.

literal: Emperor Wu did not consent; he appointed Jia Xianzhi governor and sent him at the head of troops to take the province.
idiomatic: Emperor Wu did not consent; he appointed Jia Xianzhi governor and sent him at the head of troops to take the province.

literal: Jun's defenses were strict and thorough; Xianzhi feared him, and when he reached Dong Commandery he dared not advance.
idiomatic: Cai Jun's defenses were strict and thorough; Xianzhi feared him, and when he reached Dong Commandery he dared not advance.

literal: During Tianping he served as Area Commander; he followed the army superintendent Lou Zhao in attacking Fan Zihu at Yan Province, and again with the mobile office commander Yuan Zisi suppressed Yuan Qinghe — both were pacified.
idiomatic: During Tianping he served as area commander; he followed the army superintendent Lou Zhao in attacking Fan Zihu at Yan Province, and again with the mobile office commander Yuan Zisi suppressed Yuan Qinghe — both were pacified.

literal: When Hou Shen rebelled, Jun was again made Grand Area Commander, led troops to suppress him, and Shen was defeated and fled.
idiomatic: When Hou Shen rebelled, Cai Jun was again made grand area commander, led troops to suppress him, and Shen was defeated and fled.

literal: He was again transferred to Governor of Yang Province.
idiomatic: He was again transferred to governor of Yang Province.

literal: In autumn of the third year of Tianping he died in office, aged forty-two.
idiomatic: In autumn of the third year of Tianping he died in office, aged forty-two.

literal: Posthumously he was granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Area Commander, Governor of Ji Province, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Duke of Works; his posthumous title was Majestic and Martial.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted bearer of the staff of authority, palace attendant, area commander, governor of Ji Province, director of the masters of writing, and duke of works; his posthumous title was Majestic and Martial.

literal: When Qi received the abdication, an edict ordered sacrifice announced at his tomb.
idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, an edict ordered sacrifice announced at his tomb.

literal: At the beginning of Huangjian he was given associated sacrifice in the Grand Ancestor's temple court.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Huangjian he was given associated sacrifice in Gao Huan's temple court.

literal: Han Xian, styled Puxian, was a native of Shimen in Guangning.
idiomatic: Han Xian, styled Puxian, was a native of Shimen in Guangning.

literal: He was robust and had martial ability.
idiomatic: He was robust and had martial ability.

literal: At first he followed Ge Rong in rebellion; when Ge was broken he went with the rest to Bing Province, and Erzhu Rong selected him to fill out his personal guard.
idiomatic: At first he followed Ge Rong in rebellion; when Ge was broken he went with the rest to Bing Province, and Erzhu Rong selected him to fill out his personal guard.

literal: When Rong's wife and children fled north, Shilong and others enthroned Yuan Ye, Prince of Changguang of Wei, as sovereign; Xian was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance and Colonel of Garrison Cavalry.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong's wife and children fled north, Shilong and others enthroned Yuan Ye, Prince of Changguang of Wei, as sovereign; Han Xian was appointed general who pacifies the distance and colonel of garrison cavalry.

literal: Earlier, when Shilong and others attacked Jian Province and Shicheng, Xian had military merit in both.
idiomatic: Earlier, when Shilong and others attacked Jian Province and Shicheng, Han Xian had military merit in both.

literal: Erzhu Dulü employed him as a headquarters area commander and enfeoffed him as Count of Fenyang County with a fief of four hundred households.
idiomatic: Erzhu Dulü employed him as a headquarters area commander and enfeoffed him as count of Fenyang County with a fief of four hundred households.

literal: At the beginning of Putai he was appointed General of the Forward Army and Governor of Guang Province.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Putai he was appointed general of the forward army and governor of Guang Province.

literal: Just then the Grand Ancestor raised righteousness; Dulü, because Xian was known to be acquainted with the Grand Ancestor, feared he might turn, and sent messengers to summon him.
idiomatic: Just then Gao Huan raised righteousness; Dulü, because Han Xian was known to be acquainted with Gao Huan, feared he might turn, and sent messengers to summon him.

literal: Xian did not wish to answer the summons; he secretly sent out tribal allies to raise many beacon fires, as though invaders were about to arrive.
idiomatic: Han Xian did not wish to answer the summons; he secretly sent out tribal allies to raise many beacon fires, as though invaders were about to arrive.

literal: The messengers then reported on it and were allowed to halt.
idiomatic: The messengers then reported on it and were allowed to halt.

literal: Xian still secretly sent envoys to declare his loyalty to the Grand Ancestor.
idiomatic: Han Xian still secretly sent envoys to declare his loyalty to Gao Huan.

literal: When the Grand Ancestor entered Luoyang, Erzhu offices and ranks were as a rule all struck off; because Xian had long sent pledges of loyalty, he was ordered restored to his former status.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan entered Luoyang, Erzhu offices and ranks were as a rule all struck off; because Han Xian had long sent pledges of loyalty, he was ordered restored to his former status.

literal: At the beginning of Taichang he rose through appointments to General of the Central Army and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and went out as Governor of Jian Province.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Taichang he rose through appointments to general of the central army and grand master of splendid happiness, and went out as governor of Jian Province.

literal: When Emperor Wu entered the west, Xian was transferred to administer Jing Province affairs.
idiomatic: When Emperor Wu entered the west, Han Xian was transferred to administer Jing Province affairs.

literal: At the beginning of Tianping he became Governor of Luo Province.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianping he became governor of Luo Province.

literal: The commoner Han Mulan and others led local people in rebellion; Xian defeated them and personally went about inspecting, intending to collect weapons and armor.
idiomatic: The commoner Han Mulan and others led local people in rebellion; Han Xian defeated them and personally went about inspecting, intending to collect weapons and armor.

literal: One bandit, cornered, hid among the corpses; when he saw Xian approaching he suddenly rose and hacked at him, severing his shanks, and Xian died.
idiomatic: One bandit, cornered, hid among the corpses; when he saw Han Xian approaching he suddenly rose and hacked at him, severing his shanks, and Han Xian died.

literal: Though Xian was a military man, his nature was upright and direct, and he was not greatly greedy or violent; in the places he held office, though there was no notable good governance, officials and commoners were not made to suffer.
idiomatic: Though Han Xian was a military man, his nature was upright and direct, and he was not greatly greedy or violent; in the places he held office, though there was no notable good governance, officials and commoners were not made to suffer.

literal: In the time of Emperor Ming of Han, the Western Regions sent Buddhist sutras to Luoyang borne on a white horse, and thereby White Horse Temple was founded; the sutra casket passed down at this temple was simple and unadorned in form, and the world regarded it as an ancient relic treasured through the generations.
idiomatic: In the time of Emperor Ming of Han, the Western Regions sent Buddhist sutras to Luoyang borne on a white horse, and thereby White Horse Temple was founded; the sutra casket passed down at this temple was simple and unadorned in form, and the world regarded it as an ancient relic treasured through the generations.

literal: Xian for no reason hacked it apart; before long he died, and commentators some said Xian brought calamity upon himself thereby.
idiomatic: Han Xian for no reason hacked it apart; before long he died, and some commentators said he brought calamity upon himself thereby.

literal: Posthumously he was granted Palace Attendant, Bearer of the Staff of Authority, command over military affairs in the four provinces of Ding, Ying, Anping, and the rest, Grand General, Director of the Masters of Writing, Duke of Works, and Governor of Ding Province.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted palace attendant, bearer of the staff of authority, command over military affairs in the four provinces of Ding, Ying, Anping, and the rest, grand general, director of the masters of writing, duke of works, and governor of Ding Province.

literal: His son Yi succeeded.
idiomatic: His son Yi succeeded.

literal: Wei Zhangming was a native of Dina in Tai'an.
idiomatic: Wei Zhangming was a native of Dina in Tai'an.

literal: His father Xian was General Who Pacifies the Distance in Wei and Administrator of Dai Commandery.
idiomatic: His father Xian was general who pacifies the distance in Wei and administrator of Dai Commandery.

literal: Zhangming by nature was gentle and generous, with capacity and discernment.
idiomatic: Wei Zhangming by nature was gentle and generous, with capacity and discernment.

literal: During the turmoil of Fuyang he took refuge in Taiyuan.
idiomatic: During the turmoil of Fuyang he took refuge in Taiyuan.

literal: When the Grand Ancestor was about to establish the great cause, Zhangming took part in planning; he followed the Grand Ancestor in defeating the Four Huns at Hanling and was appointed General Who Pacifies the South.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan was about to establish the great cause, Wei Zhangming took part in planning; he followed Gao Huan in defeating the Four Huns at Hanling and was appointed general who pacifies the south.

literal: When Fan Zihu seized Yan Province in rebellion, Zhangming was appointed Grand Area Commander of the Southeast Circuit and with the various armies suppressed and pacified the rebellion.
idiomatic: When Fan Zihu seized Yan Province in rebellion, Wei Zhangming was appointed grand area commander of the southeast circuit and with the various armies suppressed and pacified the rebellion.

literal: He was transferred to garrison Fanyang city, and at the same post was appointed Governor of You Province, supervising affairs in An and Ping provinces.
idiomatic: He was transferred to garrison Fanyang city, and at the same post was appointed governor of You Province, supervising affairs in An and Ping provinces.

literal: The province lay on the northern frontier; land was wasted and people scattered; though Zhangming collected much in taxes, he yet treated the people with kindness, and a modest degree of settlement and order was achieved.
idiomatic: The province lay on the northern frontier; land was wasted and people scattered; though Wei Zhangming collected much in taxes, he yet treated the people with kindness, and a modest degree of settlement and order was achieved.

literal: Before long he left office on grounds of illness.
idiomatic: Before long he left office on grounds of illness.

literal: Not long after, he was again summoned and appointed Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Area Commander over military affairs in the four provinces of Xiyan, You, Cang, and Ying, and Governor of You Province.
idiomatic: Not long after, he was again summoned and appointed grand general of chariots and cavalry, area commander over military affairs in the four provinces of Xiyan, You, Cang, and Ying, and governor of You Province.

literal: He died in office.
idiomatic: He died in office.

literal: He was posthumously granted his former offices with the addition of Minister of Works; his posthumous title was Martial and Strong.
idiomatic: He was posthumously granted his former offices with the addition of minister of works; his posthumous title was Martial and Strong.

literal: His son Xingjing was skilled with bow and horse, had martial arts, and the Grand Ancestor brought him in as a headquarters area commander.
idiomatic: His son Xingjing was skilled with bow and horse, had martial arts, and Gao Huan brought him in as a headquarters area commander.

literal: He went out as staff officer in the household of the Duke of Changshan and was granted the rank of Count of Jizhong County.
idiomatic: He went out as staff officer in the household of the Duke of Changshan and was granted the rank of count of Jizhong County.

literal: The commoners of Jin Province, Li Xiaoxing and others, gathered in bands as bandits; Xingjing followed the Duke of Works Han Gui in suppressing and pacifying them, and his rank was advanced to Marquis.
idiomatic: The commoners of Jin Province, Li Xiaoxing and others, gathered in bands as bandits; Xingjing followed the Duke of Works Han Gui in suppressing and pacifying them, and his rank was advanced to marquis.

literal: When the Grand Ancestor attacked the Emperor Wen of Zhou at Mount Mang, Xingjing was struck by a stray arrow in battle and died.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan attacked the Emperor Wen of Zhou at Mount Mang, Xingjing was struck by a stray arrow in battle and died.
